findings.reason: the section as written dispatches a worker to a gate its own mechanism cannot meet, and the honest outcome is a recorded failure whose "repair becomes a new section" for a cause §7 attributes to work that already landed.
findings.text: §7's gate ("every `/_index` request answers 200 in under 1 s in both passes") cannot be produced by the persisted-index mechanism it rests on, because the reuse path reads and sha256-hashes every covered file before it can decide to reuse a row: `_content_digest(path)` runs once per covered file ahead of the reuse branch in `metadata_index.build_index` (`reckon/metadata_index.py:506`), and its memo (`reckon/metadata_index.py:593-622`) is in-process only, so a restart clears it and the first `/_index` per project re-reads the whole tree — the persisted index saves the *parse*, not the *read*. §3's landed evidence measures this path by counting parses through `_parse_meta_uncached` (plan comment at line 358: "a post-restart rebuild of a 200-document project parses 0 files"), which is true and does not bear on the read cost §7's wall-clock gate measures. Measured 2026-10-22 on the review node: a serial read+sha256 sweep of just the HTML files (figures excluded) takes 5.5 s for reckon's 1,655 files and 10.7 s for all four projects' 4,286 files, against a per-request bound of 1 s — so the cheapest named project already exceeds the gate by 5× before any parse of a changed file.

findings.reason: a control whose two arms both fail shows nothing about the removal, so the node's negative control would report a guard firing that is not firing, which is the one thing a negative control exists to prevent.
findings.text: §7's `/_index` control says the unmutated restart "is measured as the baseline arm" and that removing the persisted index makes the baseline's gate fail, but the baseline arm faces the same digest sweep, so it fails the same 1 s gate for a reason unrelated to the removal — the red is not attributable; §12 (line 261) shows the house convention of naming exactly this case ("a base arm that reads zero is recorded as uninformative rather than as a failed control"), and §7 states no equivalent rule for a baseline arm that is red.
